From Wiktionary, the free dictionary

Translingual

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Abbreviation of English Pali or Sanskrit पालि (pāli).

Symbol

[edit]

pli

  1. (international standards) ISO 639-2 & ISO 639-3 language code for Pali.

See also

[edit]
  • Wiktionary’s coverage of Pali terms

Danish

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

pli c (singular definite plien, not used in plural form)

  1. decency, good manners
    • 2015, Haidi Wigger Klaris, Dæmonherskerens arving #1: Skyggernes Bog, Tellerup A/S, →ISBN:
      Hun tøvede, men til sidst overvandt nysgerrigheden dog alligevel plien.
      She hesitated, but ultimately, curiosity did defeat good manners after all.

Esperanto

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From French plus. Doublet of plu and plus.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /pli/
  • Audio 1:(file)
  • Audio 2:(file)
  • Rhymes: -i
  • Syllabification: pli

Adverb

[edit]

pli

  1. more
    • 1903, L. L. Zamenhof, Fundamenta Krestomatio‎[1]:
      Du homoj povas pli multe fari ol unu.
      Two people can do much more than one.

Antonyms

[edit]
  • malpli

Further reading

[edit]
  • “pli”, in Plena Ilustrita Vortaro de Esperanto [Complete Illustrated Dictionary of Esperanto], 2020, →ISBN
  • “pli”, in Reta Vortaro [Online Dictionary] (in Esperanto), 1997-2026

Faroese

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [pliː]

Noun

[edit]

pli n

  1. young seagull
  2. cry of a seagull

Coordinate terms

[edit]
  • (young seagull): mási

Interjection

[edit]

pli

  1. cry of a seagull
    másin sigur pli
    the seagull says pli

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From the verb plier.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /pli/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Toulouse)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

pli m (plural plis)

  1. fold
  2. pleat
  3. letter
  4. (card games) trick

Derived terms

[edit]
  • prendre le pli

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Swedish: pli

Further reading

[edit]
  • “pli”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Etymology

pli

  1. more

Related terms

Middle French

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • plet
  • ploy
  • ply

Etymology

[edit]

Old French ploi, from the verb ploiier, from the Latin verb plicō (“to fold”).

Noun

[edit]

pli m

  1. fold
    • 1607, Loys d'Orleans, Les ouvertures des Parlements, page 332:
      Car Macrobe se moque de luy d'avoir fait adiourner un homme pour luy auoir defait un des plis de sa robe.
      Because Macrobe is making fun of him for having adjourned the case of a man because he removed one of the folds from his robes.

Descendants

[edit]
  • → English: ply
  • French: pli

References

[edit]
  • Frédéric Godefroy (1880–1902), “pli”, in Dictionnaire de l’ancienne langue française et de tous ses dialectes du IXe au XVe siècle […], Paris: F[riedrich] Vieweg; Émile Bouillon, →OCLC.

Romansh

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin plus.

Adverb

[edit]

pli

  1. more

Swedish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French pli. Attested since 1825.

Noun

[edit]

pli c

  1. (instilled) strict, disciplined behavior
    få pli på hunden
    get the dog to behave
    få pli på någon
    get someone in line
    Hon har ingen pli på hunden
    She has no control over the dog
    Det har alltid varit pli på honom
    He's always been well-behaved

Declension

[edit]
Declension of pli
nominative genitive
singular indefinite pli plis
definite plin plins
plural indefinite — —
definite — —

References

[edit]
  • “pli”, in Svensk ordbok [Dictionary of Swedish] (in Swedish)
  • “pli”, in Svenska Akademiens ordlista [Wordlist of the Swedish Academy] (in Swedish)
  • “pli”, in Svenska Akademiens ordbok [Dictionary of the Swedish Academy] (in Swedish)
